title: B.Cu logo footprint must have a routing keepout or be assigned to GND — functional copper must not cross it
rule: Every board that carries the cec:CEC_Logo_Copper footprint (ref LOGO1, layer B.Cu) must either: (a) have a rule-area via/track keepout covering the logo bounding box so the router cannot place tracks or vias through it, OR (b) have the footprint assigned to the GND net so any copper contact is a same-net touch (not a short). Neither condition causes a DRC short. Violating both (logo with no net + no keepout + a B.Cu track crossing it) produces 4 DRC violations and was the blocker that prevented a clean route on the EPS and was identified as the open finishing item after routing.
scope: any footprint on the board whose ref matches LOGO* or whose footprint libid contains 'CEC_Logo'; the keepout bbox is the courtyard of that footprint instance
rationale: The logo is bare exposed copper on B.Cu. Without a keepout or GND assignment the autorouter routes signals through it, creating copper-copper DRC violations (via_dangling + clearance hits). This was confirmed as 4 real DRC violations on the routed EPS candidate and explicitly called out as 'LOGO1 B.Cu no-via keepout / GND-assign (clears the 4)' in the active action items.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, ROUTE-TO-CLEAN entry: 'STILL OPEN (placement/finishing, unchanged): (c) LOGO1 B.Cu no-via keepout / GND-assign (clears the 4)'; also: 'DRC=4 floor (gates pass), the 4 residual being only LOGO1 + the 2 shield-tab unconn (both placement/finishing, NOT routing)'
check_method: Parse board footprints; find any ref matching LOGO* or libid containing 'CEC_Logo'. Check: (1) is a rule_area keepout present whose polygon contains the logo bbox, OR (2) does any fp_poly in the footprint carry a net assignment to GND? If neither, flag as violation.

title: B.Cu logo must not be placed under the ESP32 PCB antenna keepout zone
rule: The LOGO1 footprint must not overlap the ESP32 module's antenna keepout region (the courtyard lobe extending beyond the pad rows on the antenna side, typically ~20mm x 10mm). Placing the logo under the antenna blocks B.Cu routing escape from the ESP pads, as happened on the first EPS routing iteration.
scope: LOGO* footprint on any board carrying an ESP32-S3-MINI-1 or ESP32-C6-MINI-1 or ESP32-S3-WROOM-1; the antenna keepout bbox is cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox(esp_libid, x, y, rot, drop_keepout=False) minus cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox(esp_libid, x, y, rot, drop_keepout=True)
rationale: Placing the logo under the ESP antenna keepout lobe forces B.Cu routing to detour around both the ESP keepout and the logo copper, eliminating the natural B.Cu escape from the ESP underside. This was explicitly identified as a real routing blocker: 'move the B.Cu CEC LOGO off the ESP underside (it blocks the natural B.Cu escape)'.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, PCBNEW REAL-COPPER ROUTING TOOLKIT entry: '(->placement) move the B.Cu CEC LOGO off the ESP underside (it blocks the natural B.Cu escape)'
check_method: Compute antenna keepout bbox of the ESP32 module instance. Compute LOGO1 bbox. Check bbox overlap. Flag if they intersect.
existing_checker: cec_pcb.courtyard_bbox (drop_keepout parameter derives the antenna lobe)

title: Every board must carry at least 3 fiducials for SMT assembly registration
rule: Each produced board must have a minimum of 3 fiducial marks (ref FID1, FID2, FID3), footprint cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm, on F.Cu, with attributes board_only / exclude_from_pos_files / exclude_from_bom. Fewer than 3 is a DFM advisory. The standard placement is 2 near the top-right + bottom-right logic side and 1 on the connector/bottom edge or lower-centre.
scope: all produced boards; derivable by counting refs matching FID* with footprint containing 'Fiducial'
rationale: The generalized Stage-1 requirement 'fiducials' defaults to 3 for SMT assembly registration. All boards that have been brought to BOM-complete state (12VHPWR Standard, Hub Standard) carry FID1/FID2/FID3. The cec_synth_pipeline.py place_mechanical() emits exactly 3 by default.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, 12VHPWR BOM entry: 'fiducials DONE 2026-06-06 (3x cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm, board_only/excl-BOM/excl-pos, refs on F.Fab: FID1 (162.25,61) TR, FID2 (166,135.5) BR, FID3 (139,116) lower-center)'; cec_synth_pipeline.py Requirement('fiducials', ..., default='3')
check_method: Count footprints with ref matching FID[0-9]* and libid containing 'Fiducial'. Flag if count < 3.

title: Fiducial footprints must carry board_only / exclude_from_pos_files / exclude_from_bom attributes
rule: Every FID* footprint must have the KiCad attributes: board_only, exclude_from_pos_files, exclude_from_bom. A fiducial appearing in the CPL or BOM export is a fab-output error.
scope: all footprints whose ref matches FID*
rationale: Fiducials are board-only assembly aids; including them in BOM or CPL files corrupts fab outputs. The cec_synth_pipeline.py chk_bom_complete explicitly skips 'FID' prefixes as non-BOM refs.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, 12VHPWR BOM entry: '3x cec-Fiducial:Fiducial_1mm_Mask2mm, board_only/excl-BOM/excl-pos'; cec_synth_pipeline.py line 451: 'if ref.startswith(("#", "TP", "FID", "LOGO", "H", "MK")): # non-BOM refs'
check_method: For each FID* footprint in the PCB, check the attr field contains board_only + exclude_from_pos_files + exclude_from_bom. Flag any missing attribute.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline.chk_bom_complete (skips FID* by prefix, so a FID that lacks exclude_from_bom and has an LCSC prop would be caught as unexpected sourcing)

title: Fiducials must not overlap any functional footprint courtyard
rule: FID* footprints require a clear zone (the 2mm soldermask opening + a ~2.5mm optical clearance ring) around them. No functional footprint courtyard may overlap within 2.5mm of any fiducial centre.
scope: all FID* footprints; clearance measured from fiducial centre to any non-fiducial/non-mounting footprint courtyard edge
rationale: The optical-registration camera needs an unobstructed view of the fiducial copper and its soldermask opening. The cec_synth_pipeline.py place_mechanical legalize_pack() call nudges fiducials to free slots 'clear of the connectors'. The fiducial footprint itself has a solder_mask_margin=0.5mm giving a 2mm opening.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, SYNTHESIS PIPELINE placer entry: 'nudge the mounts/fiducials to the nearest free spot clear of the connectors'; cec_synth_pipeline.py place_mechanical(): 'legalize_pack(anchors, [r for r in mech_pos if r in anchors], anchor_cy, W, H, clr=0.5)'
check_method: For each FID* footprint at (x,y), check that no non-mechanical footprint courtyard bbox centre is within 2.5mm. A courtyard overlap DRC hit on a fiducial also counts.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline.chk_courtyard_overlap (catches DRC courtyard_overlap, which includes fiducial overlap)

title: Logo footprint must carry board_only / exclude_from_pos_files / exclude_from_bom / allow_missing_courtyard attributes
rule: The cec:CEC_Logo_Copper footprint (ref LOGO*) must have attributes: board_only, exclude_from_pos_files, exclude_from_bom, allow_missing_courtyard. Missing allow_missing_courtyard causes a DRC courtyard warning; the others cause fab-output contamination.
scope: all footprints whose ref matches LOGO* or whose libid contains 'CEC_Logo'
rationale: The logo footprint has no courtyard (intentional, set allow_missing_courtyard) and no pads, so it must never appear in CPL/BOM/pos files. The footprint description in lib/cec.pretty/CEC_Logo_Copper.kicad_mod already sets these attributes; a board instance that overrides them would corrupt fab outputs.
source: modules/eps-8pin/eps8pin-module.kicad_pcb line 9368: '(attr exclude_from_pos_files exclude_from_bom allow_missing_courtyard board_only)'; lib/cec.pretty/CEC_Logo_Copper.kicad_mod line 8: '(attr exclude_from_pos_files exclude_from_bom allow_missing_courtyard board_only)'
check_method: For each LOGO* footprint, parse the attr field for all four required flags. Flag any missing.

title: Component values must be on F.SilkS (not silently defaulted to F.Fab)
rule: For every BOM-included component, the Value property must be placed on the F.SilkS layer (not F.Fab, which is non-plotted). KiCad footprints default Value to F.Fab; the generator's place() function rewrites it to F.SilkS. Any footprint whose Value remains on F.Fab will be invisible on the assembled board.
scope: all BOM-included footprints (i.e. excluding FID*, LOGO*, H*, TP*, MK*); check the Value property layer field
rationale: CLAUDE.md explicitly records: 'footprints default the Value to the footprint name on the non-plotted F.Fab layer, so values never showed on the board — place() rewrites the Value property to the netlist value and moves it to F.SilkS'. Without this, assembled boards have no visible value labels.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, interposer-module PCB floorplans entry: 'The generator now also writes each part\'s VALUE onto F.SilkS (v3.4): footprints default the Value to the footprint name on the non-plotted F.Fab layer, so values never showed on the board — place() rewrites the Value property to the netlist value and moves it to F.SilkS (Reference stays on silk)'
check_method: For each non-excluded footprint in the PCB, check that the 'Value' property is on layer 'F.SilkS'. Count how many remain on 'F.Fab'. Report fraction.

title: Silk text must not overlap exposed pads (silk_over_copper is filtered as cosmetic but must be reviewed before fab)
rule: Silk text (Reference or Value) must not overlap any SMD or PTH pad copper. The DRC type silk_over_copper is classified as cosmetic in this pipeline (filtered from structural DRC count) but must be resolved before gerber submission. Dense clusters from F.SilkS values will produce silk overlap warnings; these require a GUI silk-refinement pass before fab.
scope: all footprint Reference and Value text properties on F.SilkS or B.SilkS; any F.SilkS text overlapping pad copper on F.Cu
rationale: The pipeline explicitly classifies silk_overlap, silk_over_copper, and silk_edge_clearance as cosmetic DRC types that are excluded from gate counts. CLAUDE.md notes 'This adds silk-overlap warnings on the dense clusters (a GUI silk-refinement task)'. These must be cleared before fab.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, PCB floorplans entry: 'This adds silk-overlap warnings on the dense clusters (a GUI silk-refinement task)'; cec_synth_pipeline.py COSMETIC tuple: '"silk_overlap", "silk_over_copper", "silk_edge_clearance"'
check_method: Run kicad-cli DRC and count silk_overlap + silk_over_copper + silk_edge_clearance violations. Any non-zero count is a pre-fab advisory.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline (COSMETIC filter — these are filtered FROM the gate count, not checked for zero; a separate pre-fab check would need to count them)

title: M3 mounting holes must be tied to GND (chassis-grounded)
rule: All M3 mounting holes (footprint MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via, refs H1..H4 on the Hub, H1..H3 on modules) must be on the GND net — specifically the pad via type (not NPTH bare hole). The copper pad + via provides the chassis-to-PCB-GND bond. Any mounting hole without a GND net is a chassis-isolation error.
scope: all footprints whose libid contains 'MountingHole' and whose ref matches H[0-9]* or MK*; check that each has at least one pad connected to GND
rationale: CLAUDE.md records '4x M3 chassis-grounded mounting' for Hub Standard and the spec table states 'Mounting: 4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (PC-standard fastener; MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via)'. The cec_synth_pipeline.py uses _MOUNT_FP = 'cec-MountingHole:MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via' — the pad+via variant, not bare NPTH.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §Hub Standard table: 'Mounting | 4x M3 corner holes, chassis-grounded (PC-standard fastener; MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via)'; CLAUDE.md: '4x M3 chassis-grounded mounting'; cec_synth_pipeline.py: '_MOUNT_FP = "cec-MountingHole:MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via"'
check_method: For each MountingHole footprint in the netlist, verify it appears on the GND net. Flag any mounting hole with no net or a non-GND net.

title: Hub boards must carry exactly 4 M3 corner mounting holes
rule: Hub Standard and Hub Pro must carry exactly 4 M3 mounting holes (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via), placed at or near the four board corners. Modules must carry 3 M3 holes (2 on the logic/RJ-45 side + 1 on the connector/cable side, or the Stage-1 elicited pattern).
scope: hubs: boards in hubs/*/; modules: boards in modules/*/; count footprints matching _MOUNT_FP by board path
rationale: Spec table for Hub Standard: '4x M3 corner holes'. CLAUDE.md for modules: '3 M3 mounts (2 left strip, 1 bottom-right below the RJ-45)' and PCIe: 'TWO on the logic/right side (TR/BR corners) + ONE centered on the connector/left side'. The generalized Stage-1 default is '3_2logic_1conn'.
source: CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §Hub Standard table: 'Mounting | 4x M3 corner holes'; CLAUDE.md, Done section, EPS condensed: '3 M3 mounts (2 left strip, 1 bottom-right below the RJ-45)'; cec_synth_pipeline.py Requirement('mount_holes', default='3_2logic_1conn')
check_method: Count footprints with libid containing 'MountingHole_3.2mm_M3' per board. Hubs: flag if count != 4. Modules: flag if count < 3.

title: Hub Standard PCB must be 4-layer 1.6mm ENIG matte-black
rule: The Hub Standard board stackup must specify: 4-layer, 1.6mm total thickness, ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold) surface finish, matte black solder mask. The stackup recorded in the .kicad_pcb must match (4 copper layers, the outer copper at 2oz, inners at 1oz).
rationale: Locked in CLAUDE.md: '4-layer 1.6 mm ENIG matte-black PCB'. Also in the spec table: 'PCB | 4-layer 1.6 mm, ENIG, matte black'.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard description: '4-layer 1.6 mm ENIG matte-black PCB'; CEC-Platform-Ground-Truth-Spec.md §Hub Standard table: 'PCB | 4-layer 1.6 mm, ENIG, matte black'
check_method: Parse the (setup (stackup ...)) block in the .kicad_pcb. Count copper layers (must be 4). Check thickness (must sum to ~1.6mm). ENIG and matte-black are fab notes, not machine-readable in KiCad, so partial check only.

title: SW* button 2-pad footprints produce a known-false mask-bridge DRC hit under kicad-cli headless; do not treat as real
rule: The TS-1088-AR02016 2-pad button footprint (SW1, SW2) produces a single mask_bridge / shorting_items false-positive DRC violation under kicad-cli headless mode that is geometrically impossible and does not appear in the KiCad GUI. This arises from the way headless DRC handles the 2-pad SMD land without solder mask expansion context. A checker must suppress this specific violation type (mask_bridge on a SW* footprint) before counting structural DRC errors.
scope: footprints whose ref matches SW[0-9]* and whose footprint contains 'TS-1088' or 'AR02016'; DRC violation type mask_bridge or shorting_items on those refs
rationale: CLAUDE.md records the exact artifact: '1 known headless false SW2 mask-bridge artifact (geometrically impossible; absent in GUI)' on the PCIe-2port and PCIe-3port condensed boards.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, PCIe condensed candidate generator entry: 'Both DRC 0 structural except 1 known headless false SW2 mask-bridge artifact (geometrically impossible; absent in GUI)'
check_method: After running kicad-cli DRC, filter out any violation whose type is mask_bridge or shorting_items AND whose items reference a footprint matching SW[0-9]* with libid containing 'TS-1088' or 'AR02016'. Count remaining structural violations.

title: SK6812 LED footprint rotation can yield false within-footprint pad-short DRC hits under kicad-cli headless
rule: Rotating SK6812 MINI-E LED footprints (refs DL*) can produce false within-footprint pad-short or mask-bridge DRC violations when checked headlessly with kicad-cli. These do not appear in the GUI. A checker must cross-check with a render and must not count these as real structural violations.
scope: footprints whose ref matches DL[0-9]* or whose libid contains 'SK6812'
rationale: CLAUDE.md states: 'Known kicad-cli artifact: rotating a footprint\'s text can yield FALSE within-footprint pad-short / mask-bridge DRC hits headlessly (seen on the SK6812 LEDs). Cross-check a render before believing them — they do not appear in the GUI.'
source: CLAUDE.md, What Claude should do section: 'Known kicad-cli artifact: rotating a footprint\'s text can yield FALSE within-footprint pad-short / mask-bridge DRC hits headlessly (seen on the SK6812 LEDs).'
check_method: After running kicad-cli DRC, filter out any violation of type shorting_items or mask_bridge where all referenced items belong to the same SK6812 footprint. Verify with a render that the violation is a text-rotation artifact.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline.COSMETIC (silk_overlap included; the pad-short itself is not in the cosmetic filter — this specific artifact needs its own filter rule)

title: Stale copper zone fill produces false shorts after footprint moves under kicad-cli — must purge filled_polygon blocks
rule: After any footprint placement change in a .kicad_pcb with pre-existing filled copper zones, the (filled_polygon) blocks must be purged (or the zone left unfilled) before running kicad-cli DRC. Stale fill reads as real copper under the new footprint and generates false clearance/short violations. kicad-cli cannot refill zones; only the GUI (B key) or the real ZONE_FILLER (via pcbnew.ZONE_FILLER) can regenerate fill.
scope: any .kicad_pcb that has been edited programmatically (footprint position changed) and still contains (filled_polygon) blocks; checkable by comparing zone fill timestamp vs footprint edit timestamps
rationale: CLAUDE.md records: 'kicad-cli cannot refill zones. Moving a footprint under a filled pour leaves stale fill that DRC reads as a false short; clear the stale (filled_polygon) blocks (or leave the zone unfilled) and tell the user to re-fill with B in the GUI.' Also noted for the 12VHPWR PCB: 'the 252 actual 0.000mm clearance/hole hits are STALE GND-pour, NOT real shorts'.
source: CLAUDE.md What Claude should do: 'kicad-cli cannot refill zones. Moving a footprint under a filled pour leaves stale fill that DRC reads as a false short'; active action item 4: 'the 252 "actual 0.000mm" clearance/hole hits are STALE GND-pour, NOT real shorts'
check_method: Check whether any zone in the .kicad_pcb has non-empty (filled_polygon) content AND the board was generated/modified programmatically. If so, warn that DRC results may contain stale-zone false positives. Deterministic check: count zones with non-empty filled_polygon blocks on boards that cec_pcb.build_board() emitted (these are always emitted unfilled).

title: Test points (TP*) for GND/+3V3/+5VSB/VRAIL_DIV/CAN_H/CAN_L are recommended where board space allows
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module (and by analogy any module with an analog front-end) test points on nets GND, +3V3, +5VSB, VRAIL_DIV, CAN_H, CAN_L are recommended if board area permits. Test points are added in the GUI only (TestPoint symbol is not in the schematic); they must carry the board_only / exclude_from_pos_files / exclude_from_bom attributes. This is an advisory — omission is acceptable when space is tight.
scope: 12vhpwr-standard and any module with VRAIL_DIV net; refs TP[0-9]*
rationale: CLAUDE.md active action item 4: 'Test points recommended ONLY if room (GND/+3V3/+5VSB/VRAIL_DIV/CAN_H/CAN_L) — add in the GUI, not the schematic (TestPoint symbol isn\'t embedded).'
source: CLAUDE.md, active action item 4 (12VHPWR Standard PCB finish): 'Test points recommended ONLY if room (GND/+3V3/+5VSB/VRAIL_DIV/CAN_H/CAN_L) — add in the GUI, not the schematic (TestPoint symbol isn\'t embedded).'
check_method: For boards with VRAIL_DIV net: check if any TP* footprint is present. Report count as advisory (0 = advisory absent, >=1 = advisory met).

title: The CEC logo must be on B.Cu (back copper) — not F.Cu — on all module boards
rule: The cec:CEC_Logo_Copper footprint must be placed on B.Cu (layer attribute 'B.Cu') on all module boards and on F.Cu on the Hub Standard (which has more back-side real estate vs the module's crowded B.Cu). Modules place it on B.Cu per the generator convention. Placing it on F.Cu on a module would compete with the dense F.Cu component side.
scope: all module boards (modules/*/); the footprint layer field of the LOGO* instance
rationale: All module board instances set (layer "B.Cu") on the logo footprint (confirmed in EPS and PCIe boards). Hub Standard sets it on F.Cu. The generator comment in CLAUDE.md: 'CEC copper logo on the back' for the interposer modules.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, interposer-module PCB floorplans: 'CEC copper logo on the back'; modules/eps-8pin/eps8pin-module.kicad_pcb line 9364: '(layer "B.Cu")'; modules/pcie-8pin-2port/pcie8pin-2port-module.kicad_pcb line 9392: '(layer "B.Cu")'
check_method: For footprints in modules/ directories matching LOGO*, check the layer attribute is 'B.Cu'. For hubs/hub-standard/, check it is 'F.Cu'. Flag any mismatch.

title: M3 mounting holes must not overlap connector courtyards and must be clear of the cable-connector footprint area
rule: M3 mounting holes must be inset at least 3mm from every board edge (the _half_extent hardcoded keepout in cec_synth_pipeline.py) and must not overlap the courtyard of any cable connector (J_IN*, J_OUT*). The PCIe/EPS generators specifically note 'the cables INSET so the four corner M3 mounts stay clear of the connectors'.
scope: all H[0-9]* mounting hole footprints; check against connector footprint courtyards (refs J_IN*, J_OUT*, J3, J4)
rationale: CLAUDE.md records: 'the cables INSET so the four corner M3 mounts (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via) stay clear of the connectors'. The placer hardcodes a 3mm M3 keepout because the footprint courtyard parses as degenerate (1.73x0.0mm) in the automated pipeline.
source: CLAUDE.md, Done section, interposer-module PCB floorplans: 'the cables INSET so the four corner M3 mounts (MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via) stay clear of the connectors'; cec_synth_pipeline.py: '(b) the M3 mount courtyard PARSES DEGENERATE in cec_pcb (half 1.73x0.0) -> hardcoded a 3mm M3 keepout'
check_method: For each H* footprint at (x,y), compute a 3mm radius keepout circle. Check that no connector (J_IN*, J_OUT*, J3, J4) courtyard bbox intersects this circle. Also verify x > 3mm from left edge, x < W-3mm, y > 3mm from top, y < H-3mm.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline (legalize_pack nudges mounts clear of connectors; chk_courtyard_overlap catches if they remain overlapping)

title: Logo footprint must not be placed in the high-current power corridor (J_IN to shunt to J_OUT column)
rule: The CEC_Logo_Copper footprint must not be placed in the high-current copper corridor defined by the bounding box between the PSU-side connector (J_IN) and the load-side connector (J_OUT), covering the shunt row. This corridor is reserved for 12V power pours and thermal copper; bare copper from the logo in this region would create ambiguous copper islands that the ZONE_FILLER might merge with power pours.
scope: module boards with high-current paths (eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*, 12vhpwr-*); the corridor is derived from the J_IN/J_OUT connector bboxes projected across the board
rationale: The automated routing work identified that the logo must be kept off the B.Cu routing escape zones. Placing the logo in the 12V corridor would compete with the high-current pour geometry. The 'considerations list' in CLAUDE.md action item -2 includes 'high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation' as a constraint the placer must honor.
source: CLAUDE.md, active action item -2: 'the design pass must add: (1) high-current corridor keepout + pour reservation'; also the EPS loop iteration: '(->placement) move U2 next to the ESP CAN pads w/ C3/C6 displaced; CEC logo moved off the ESP underside -> B.Cu freed'
check_method: Derive the high-current corridor bbox from J_IN and J_OUT connector pad positions (min/max x of the 12V pad columns, full board height). Check that no LOGO* footprint bbox overlaps this corridor.

title: RJ-45 FTP jack shield-tab pads (SH1/SH2) must not have silk text crossing them
rule: The Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C FTP jack (J1 on modules, J2-J5 on the Hub) has two extra shield-tab pads (SH1, SH2) beyond the 8 signal pads. Silk text from adjacent components or from the reference label must not overlap these pads. Silk-over-pad on the shield tabs causes solderability issues at the grounding point.
scope: footprints with libid containing 'RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal' or ref J1/J2/J3/J4/J5 on Hub; check F.SilkS or B.SilkS text bbox against the SH1/SH2 pad positions
rationale: CLAUDE.md active action item 3 for Hub Standard PCB: 'silk cleanup on the RJ-45 shield pads + board-edge silk'. The shield tabs are new relative to the original unshielded footprint and their pad positions may attract silk from the reference or from adjacent parts.
source: CLAUDE.md, active action item 3 (Hub Standard PCB pre-fab layout): 'silk cleanup on the RJ-45 shield pads + board-edge silk'
check_method: For each RJ45_FTP footprint, parse pad positions for SH1 and SH2. Check whether any F.SilkS gr_text or fp_text bbox overlaps these pad copper areas. Flag overlaps.
existing_checker: cec_synth_pipeline.COSMETIC (silk_over_copper is filtered as cosmetic — this constraint elevates it to a pre-fab advisory specifically for shield-tab pads)
